title: EGMA: Enhancing Data Reuse and Workload Balancing in Message Passing GNN Acceleration via Gram Matrix Optimization
problem: Message-passing GNNs perform vertex and edge operations dependent on graph structure that cannot be characterized as traditional sparse-dense or general matrix multiplications, making existing matrix-based data reuse and workload balancing optimizations ineffective.
motivation: Efficient GNN acceleration is critical as GNNs are widely deployed for complex graph-related problems but current accelerators have limited applicability to message-passing workloads.
method: EGMA leverages Gram Matrix mathematical insights to identify and exploit data reuse and workload balancing opportunities in message-passing GNNs. The accelerator improves data locality by analyzing communication patterns through gram matrix formulation and distributes computation load evenly across processing units to balance workload distribution.
key_novelty: Using Gram Matrix optimization to simultaneously exploit data reuse and workload balancing for message-passing GNN acceleration.
contributions: Novel Gram Matrix-based optimization technique for data reuse in message-passing GNNs
EGMA accelerator architecture supporting diverse GNN models
Performance speedup of 1.57× average over prior GNN accelerators (Betty, FlowGNN, ReGNN)
Energy reduction of 32.25% average compared to existing approaches

metrics.speedup: 1.57× average (1.43× vs ReGNN, 1.57× vs Betty, 1.72× vs FlowGNN)
